title: Table races and edge cases
idea: A table race is two bookings both seeing a table free and both claiming it; the fix makes the overlap check and write one atomic step.

analogy.text: Two hosts glance at the same empty booth and both promise it to a party. A single clipboard on the booth, held by one host at a time, stops that.
analogy.breaks: A Java lock works inside one process; two servers need the database to decide.

points: Check free, then save, is two steps; another booking can slip between them.
`tryReserve` checks overlap and adds inside one `synchronized` method.
Each table has its own lock, so bookings for different tables never wait.
A loser tries the next table in best-fit order before giving up.

steps.caption: Unsafe version. P-1 asks whether T2 is free at 19:00.
Before P-1 writes, P-2 asks too. T2's schedule is still empty.
Both threads now hold the answer yes. Neither knows about the other.
P-1 adds its slot to T2.
P-2 acts on its stale yes and adds an overlapping slot. Two parties, one table.
Safe version. Both threads call `tryReserve` on T2 at once.
T2's lock lets one call in. It finds no overlap and adds P-1's slot.
P-2's call runs next, sees the overlap, and returns false.
P-2 tries the next table in best-fit order. T4 is free, so it wins there.

code.title: Prove the race
code.caption: A barrier forces both threads to check before either writes, so the double booking shows up every run. Slots are minutes since midnight here.

walk.text: Run the same race twice: unsafe first, then atomic.
Two tables in best-fit order, one 19:00 slot, a two-thread barrier.
Join both threads, then sort the tables they got, so output is stable.
Unsafe: pick a free table, wait for the other thread, then write.
Safe: try each table; `tryReserve` refuses an overlap atomically.
Every method locks this table's schedule only, so tables do not block each other.

code.title: Retry, reschedule, cancel
code.caption: Three failure cases on one table: a retried request, a move that would clash, and a cancel that frees time.

walk.text: A client times out and sends the same request key again.
Move RV-1 twice, cancel RV-2, then try the second move again.
A known key returns the first result instead of booking twice.
Reschedule ignores its own old slot; on a clash the old slot stays.
The overlap check skips one id, so a move can overlap itself.

pitfalls: Do not lock the whole restaurant; one lock per table keeps other tables bookable.
Never cancel the old slot before the new one is secured during a reschedule.
A retried booking without an Idempotency-Key can create two reservations for one party.

quiz.q: What does TableRace print on its second line?
quiz.why: One `tryReserve` on T2 wins; the other sees the overlap, returns false, and that thread reserves T4 instead. Sorting makes the order fixed.

takeaway: Check and claim a table in one atomic step, locked per table.
